title: Assignment links two variables
statement: After a = b the two variables are connected, so whenever b changes later, a changes too.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: trace a change to the source variable after an assignment between primitives
evidence_patterns.signature: reports the destination variable as having the source's new value

example.item:
a = 1
b = a
a = 7
What is b?

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip gives the wrong value once. The belief is stated ('b is a now') and holds on every item where the source is later reassigned.

vs.prog.var.assignment-is-equation: Equation believers object to x = x + 1; linkers do not.
vs.prog.obj.assignment-copies-object: The object case is the mirror image: there the learner expects independence and gets aliasing. Test with a primitive and an object item.

conflicts_with.label: Assignment copies a value into a variable at one moment

resolved_by.label: Assignment copies a value into a variable at one moment
A variable holds exactly one value at a time

sources.citation: Ma, L., Ferguson, J., Roper, M., & Wood, M. (2007). Investigating the viability of mental models held by novice programmers. In Proceedings of the 38th SIGCSE Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE '07), 499-503.
sources.note: Non-viable mental models of value assignment among novices.
